subject.title: [Bug]: agents set-identity --workspace does not set the agent's stored workspace, but its success response implies it does

question: Should the public CLI solve this by adding a dedicated existing-agent workspace setter, or by only clarifying that `set-identity --workspace` is a locator?
rationale: Both repairs are technically valid, but the choice changes public CLI semantics and JSON output compatibility, so automation should not choose it without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add Dedicated Setter
options.body: Add an `agents set-workspace` or `agents update --workspace` path backed by `agents.update`, while making `set-identity` output explicit about locator versus stored workspace.

options.title: Clarify Output Only
options.body: Keep relocation out of the CLI for now and add or rename additive output fields so `set-identity` cannot be read as confirming a stored workspace update.

options.title: Repurpose Set Identity
options.body: Make `set-identity --workspace` update stored workspace too, accepting compatibility risk against current help text, docs, and scripts.

recommendation.title: Add Dedicated Setter
recommendation.body: Add an `agents set-workspace` or `agents update --workspace` path backed by `agents.update`, while making `set-identity` output explicit about locator versus stored workspace.

likelyOwner.reason: The original identity CLI contract traces to this owner, and the remaining choice is public CLI shape rather than only the Gateway implementation.
